FLIVL CONSTANTIVS NOB C ; PROVIDENTIAE CAESS

A late Roman copper alloy nummus of the House of Constantine. The obverse depicts a bust left of Emperor Constantius II, with the inscription FLIVL CONSTANTIVS NOB C. The reverse depicts a camp or town gateway with two towers, with the inscription PROVIDENTIAE CAESS and PTR at the bottom, meaning it was struck in Trier. Struck AD 324-5
